TTGR62 – Culross & Preston Island Loop

Scenery and points of interest

Starting from Dalgety Bay Sailing Club, this enjoyable 33.9-mile circular ride explores the communities and changing landscapes of western Fife. Heading west through Rosyth and Crossford, the route makes its way towards Torryburn and Culross, combining the character of established Fife towns and villages with the coastal setting of the Firth of Forth.

The journey towards Torryburn and Culross brings the ride into one of western Fife's most distinctive areas. Culross is particularly well known for its beautifully preserved historic village centre, traditional buildings and connections with Scotland's past. The nearby Firth of Forth provides the wider geographical setting for this part of the journey, offering a contrast to the more inland sections of the ride.

After Culross, the route continues towards Newmills before turning east through Crossford and Rosyth. Passing through Inverkeithing on the final approach, the tandems return to Dalgety Bay Sailing Club to complete the circuit. With its combination of historic communities, coastal surroundings and familiar western Fife locations, this is a rewarding outing for pilots and stokers to enjoy together.

Route highlights
  • Dalgety Bay Sailing Club: The starting and finishing point for this circular western Fife adventure.
  • Rosyth and Crossford: Familiar communities marking the outward and return journeys.
  • Torryburn: A village on the northern shore of the Firth of Forth, providing a coastal element to the route.
  • Culross: A historic village celebrated for its traditional architecture and distinctive character.
  • Newmills: The western section of the circuit before the return towards Crossford.
  • Inverkeithing: The final town on the approach back to Dalgety Bay.

Terrain and cycling difficulty

Difficulty: Moderately Difficult

This 33.9-mile circular route offers a satisfying ride through western Fife, combining relatively modest changes in elevation with a distance that provides a worthwhile endurance challenge. The route's generally low-lying character makes it an appealing option for tandem teams comfortable with a longer outing, while the mixture of settlements and changing gradients calls for steady pacing and good communication.

  • Distance: Approximately 33.9 miles (54.6 km), starting and finishing at Dalgety Bay Sailing Club. Allow time for a comfortable pace, regrouping and refreshment breaks.
  • Climbing: Approximately 213 metres of cumulative ascent are estimated across the circuit. The climbing appears to be spread throughout the ride rather than concentrated in one major ascent.
  • Descending: Around 213 metres of cumulative descent are estimated. Pilots should remain attentive to changes in gradient, particularly when approaching bends, junctions or built-up areas.
  • Elevation and gradients: The route stays relatively low, with elevations ranging from approximately 3 to 48 metres above sea level. No particularly steep, sustained climb has been identified, although shorter rises may still require a timely change of gear.
  • Route character: The journey passes through Dalgety Bay, Rosyth, Crossford, Torryburn, Culross, Newmills and Inverkeithing. Pilots should be prepared for junctions, changes in direction and the need to navigate through several communities.
  • Tandem considerations: A consistent cadence and clear communication between pilot and stoker will help maintain a comfortable rhythm. With over 30 miles to cover, it is worth planning regular opportunities to rest, drink and regroup, even though the overall climbing is relatively modest.

Overall: An enjoyable, moderately difficult circuit that combines a manageable amount of climbing with the satisfaction of a longer ride through western Fife. Well suited to tandem teams looking for a varied outing without major hill climbs.
